event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: EA’s Form 10-K devotes a discrete risk-factor subsection to the COVID-19 pandemic, establishing that the virus has already had a “significant” adverse effect on the company’s operations, workforce productivity and product launch timing, while also emphasizing that these pressures could persist or intensify.  The language is largely qualitative, but it is specific, recent (within three years of the filing) and cites concrete operational consequences—e.g., delayed launches, remote-work productivity erosion, and heightened talent-retention risk—rather than generic boiler-plate.  Mitigating references (office re-openings, flexible work models) temper but do not neutralize the seriousness.  Under the Time Decay Principle, COVID-19 remains a recent event, so individual snippet scores can legitimately reach the upper mid-to-high range (7-10) when evidence shows direct, realized impact; sentences describing only potential or moderated risk score lower.  Taken together, the disclosures reveal a material, ongoing operational risk whose magnitude is meaningful but not yet quantified in dollars, warranting an overall elevated—but not maximum—risk assessment.

evidence_list.snippet: Events such as the COVID-19 pandemic and the various responses to it have previously affected and may in the future affect how we are operating our business.

components.reason: Explicitly ties COVID-19 to past operational impact (realised effect).
Projects continuing future impact, indicating ongoing risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct acknowledgement of both historical and forward-looking operational disruption gives this sentence moderate severity.

evidence_list.snippet: We are subject to unforeseen events such as the COVID-19 pandemic, which has significantly impacted, and may in the future impact, our business and results of operations.

components.reason: States COVID-19 has already ‘significantly impacted’ the business—strong wording.
Emphasises possible future impacts as well.
Frames COVID-19 as an unforeseen external shock, heightening uncontrollability.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Combines confirmation of material past impact with caution of additional future harm, producing a high (but not maximum) score.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic and the various responses to it have affected how we and our partners are operating our businesses.

components.reason: Shows pandemic impact extends beyond EA to partners, widening risk perimeter.
Uses past-tense ‘have affected,’ confirming realised disruption.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highlights supply-chain/partner dimension of pandemic impact but without quantitative detail, yielding a mid-level score.

evidence_list.snippet: As we have re-opened our offices, employees are offered more flexibility in the amount of time they work in an office.

components.reason: Indicates shift to hybrid model—evidence of operational change tied to pandemic.
Represents a mitigating measure (office re-opening and flexibility).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Describes a mitigation that offsets the operational change, netting to a neutral risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: Further, the increased availability of hybrid or remote working arrangements has expanded the pool of companies that can compete for our employees and employment candidates.

components.reason: Identifies competitive talent risk stemming from remote-work shift.
Connects directly to potential labor shortages/retention issues.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Points to a specific, pandemic-driven labor-market threat, but lacks quantified impact, so risk is moderate.

evidence_list.snippet: The long-term effects of the COVID-19 pandemic on the future of work may present operational challenges and impact our ability to attract and retain talent, and our teams’ ability to collaborate creatively, each of which may adversely affect our business.

components.reason: Flags long-term, structural operational challenges (uncertainty).
Explicitly mentions talent attraction and retention risk.
Notes potential hit to creative collaboration, core to EA’s product development.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Enumerates several critical forward-looking risks tied to pandemic-driven work changes, producing a solid mid-level score.

evidence_list.snippet: Certain of our development teams have worked for an extended period in a distributed environment, whereas these teams historically collaborated in-person on the creative and technical process required to develop high-quality products and services at scale.

components.reason: Highlights concrete shift from in-person to distributed work due to pandemic conditions.
Implies potential quality/process risk in product development.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Describes structural change but stops short of stating actual harm, so risk is noted but relatively modest.

evidence_list.snippet: This has disrupted, and may continue to disrupt, the productivity of our workforce and the creative process to which our teams are accustomed.

components.reason: Admits actual disruption to productivity (realised impact).
Warns of continued disruption going forward.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Past and potential future disruptions elevate the snippet to a moderate-high risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: Companies in our industry have experienced issues related to game and service quality associated with the period during which employees primarily worked-from-home, and we have changed the launch date of key products in part because of challenges associated with a distributed development environment.

components.reason: Cites industry-wide quality problems linked to remote work—broader context.
Discloses EA’s own product launch delays—direct material consequence.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Combines direct, realized schedule impact with evidence of systemic industry quality issues, justifying a high score.

evidence_list.snippet: The longer-term impact to our creative and technical development processes associated with more distributed work models is unknown and the associated risks, including with respect to game quality and developmental delays, which may cause us to delay or cancel additional release dates, may be heightened.

components.reason: Acknowledges heightened, uncertain long-term risks tied to remote work.
Specifically lists possible delay/cancellation of releases—material operational threat.
Mentions potential degradation of game quality.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Potential for heightened delays and quality issues pushes this forward-looking statement into the upper-mid range.

evidence_list.snippet: If we are not able to respond to and manage the impact of these and other currently unknown impacts related to events such as the COVID-19 pandemic, our business will be harmed.

components.reason: Concludes that failure to manage pandemic impacts will ‘harm’ the business—clear downside.
References unknown future impacts, underscoring uncertainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Summarizes potential harm but lacks specificity or quantification, meriting a moderate score.
